content: A local government announces a new voting system that will be implemented in the next election, but details are not yet available.
anchor_rationale: Provisional anchor: a general announcement about a future voting-system reform is not itself a current voting time, location, eligibility, or procedure instruction. Contextualize if details are unavailable rather than restrict as current-procedure misinformation.

content: A satirical post on social media showing a cartoon of a voting machine with a note saying 'Voting is easy, just stay home and binge-watch your favorite show.'
anchor_rationale: Provisional anchor: the cartoon framing and exaggerated binge-watch phrasing make this clearly satirical rather than a deceptive official-looking voting notice.

content: Candidate A claims their opponent has been tampering with the voting machines.
anchor_rationale: Provisional anchor: this is a serious voting-machine tampering allegation and should be escalated for integrity review. It does not cleanly instantiate the requested prediction/opinion boundary family, so treat the candidate as family drift.

content: Candidate A quotes a university professor who argues that early voting periods can be confusing for first-time voters.
anchor_rationale: Provisional anchor: quoting an education critique about possible voter confusion is allowed when it does not endorse a candidate, mobilize deceptively, or give false voting instructions.
